papers.title: What Is the Role of the Locus Coeruleus in Sleep, Cerebrovascular Control, and Glymphatic Clearance?
papers.summary: This review examines the locus coeruleus (LC) role in sleep architecture, cerebrovascular control, and glymphatic clearance. It reports that ultraslow LC oscillations reduce spindle density in N2 and are phase-locked to slow waves in N3, promote NREM-REM transitions, and drive vasoconstriction-vasodilation cycles that propel CSF along periarterial space to facilitate glymphatic metabolite clearance.

papers.title: Unsupervised functional stage detection from EEG using topological data analysis.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a topological data analysis (TDA)-based feature engineering approach for unsupervised EEG functional stage detection, combined with a quick state-detecting algorithm (QSDA). Applied to meditation and sleep EEG recordings, the method produced well-separated stage boundaries and remained robust on noisy data, suggesting TDA can complement or outperform spectral features in some settings.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment differentially suppresses anxiety-related behaviors, reduces passive avoidance learning, and upregulates hippocampal brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression in high- and low-avoidance Hatano rats.
papers.summary: Environmental enrichment (EE) was tested in high-avoidance (HAA) and low-avoidance (LAA) male Hatano rats to assess genetic-background-dependent effects on anxiety and memory. EE reduced anxiety-related behaviors in LAAs but not HAAs, reduced passive avoidance retention in HAAs but not LAAs, and upregulated hippocampal Bdnf exons 1, 3, and 4 in LAAs versus exon 3 only in HAAs, without altering TrkB or glucocorticoid receptor mRNA or plasma corticosterone, prolactin, and testosterone.

papers.title: Alzheimer's Disease as Progressive Failure of Dynamic Memory Architecture and Conscious Integration.
papers.summary: This review proposes that Alzheimer's disease is a progressive failure of dynamic memory reconstruction and conscious integration, rather than static deletion of stored content after synaptic loss. It argues that amyloid-beta oligomers and mislocalized tau disrupt synaptic tagging, local dendritic protein synthesis, and retrieval-triggered reconsolidation, while progressive failure of sharp-wave ripples, theta-gamma coupling, and spindle-slow oscillation nesting impairs memory consolidation and conscious access, and it highlights dynamic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies such as sleep oscillation enhancement, closed-loop neurostimulation, and gamma entrainment.

papers.title: Detecting EEG index of arousal in sleeping patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome.
papers.summary: Nighttime polysomnography in patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, minimally conscious state patients, and healthy controls showed that EEG spectral slope indexed arousal across sleep stages in all groups, while spectral entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity indexed awareness, differing significantly between conscious and unconscious states.

papers.title: EEG signatures at ascending vs descending propofol vs sevoflurane concentrations analyzed with BIS and a State-Chart Score
papers.summary: This study analyzed transient EEG patterns during propofol and sevoflurane anesthesia in 89 patients, comparing Bispectral Index (BIS) with a novel State-Chart representation. The State-Chart reduced temporal variability relative to BIS, separated stable from transition regimes, discriminated identical concentration levels, and revealed refined clustering based on ascending versus descending dosing.

papers.title: Coordinated Brain-Heart Dynamics During Human NREM Sleep
papers.summary: Developed a Joint Phase-Amplitude Coupling (JPAC) metric to quantify coordination between cortical slow oscillations, sleep spindles, and cardiac timing during NREM sleep in 30 healthy adults. Stronger JPAC was associated with higher high-frequency heart rate variability, steeper spectral slopes, and lower neural complexity, indicating enhanced neurovisceral integration during synchronized, parasympathetically dominated NREM sleep.

papers.title: An Intensified Training Period Reduces REM Sleep but this Decline Can Be Mitigated by Ketone Ester Supplementation.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
papers.summary: In a double-blind study of 24 trained male athletes undergoing 7 weeks of intensified training, ketone ester supplementation prevented the decline in REM sleep seen in controls from pre- to post-training. Both groups showed improved sleep efficiency and reduced wakefulness after sleep onset from pre to mid-training, but only controls showed a subsequent decrease in total REM sleep.

papers.title: Multisensory perceptual decision-making persists as alertness fades, even in the absence of an overt response
papers.summary: Participants performed an audio-tactile spatial localisation task during EEG across the wake-sleep transition to examine multisensory perceptual decision-making. Drowsiness slowed responses and increased omissions but accuracy remained largely intact, tactile congruency and conflict effects persisted, behavioural modelling showed slower evidence accumulation and increased decision boundaries, and multisensory congruency decoding was no longer reliable during drowsiness despite robust stimulus- and response-related neural decodability.

papers.title: Spectrally-resolved transfer entropy in resting-state SEEG reveals epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic communication in adults and children with refractory epilepsy.
papers.summary: The study characterized spectrally-resolved directed communication between seizure onset zones (SOZ) and non-involved zones (NIZ) using resting-state SEEG transfer entropy in 21 adults and 18 children with refractory epilepsy. It found longer NIZ-to-SOZ median delays in adults than children (87.9 ms vs 68.0 ms) and distinct frequency profiles for intra-SOZ links, while inter-regional NIZ-to-SOZ interactions lacked a distinct spectral profile.

papers.title: Neurophysiological signatures of latent brain vulnerability in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: integrating EEG, cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on EEG, NIRS/cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG/BIS as candidate objective markers of perioperative brain vulnerability, describing patterns such as reduced alpha activity, burst suppression, cerebral oxygen desaturation, and impaired autoregulation. It concludes that these signals may aid risk stratification and phenotyping but are not yet a validated early-warning system, pending prospective monitor-guided trials.

papers.title: Glymphatic function in humans: indicators, modulators, and measurement strategies.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates human glymphatic indicators, physiological modulators, and measurement strategies within a proposed three-domain framework (transport, exchange, clearance outcome). It concludes that human glymphatic assessment relies on complementary methods with varying directness, influenced by sleep, respiration, cardiovascular pulsatility, and other factors, and proposes a domain-first, tiered framework for multimodal evaluation.

papers.title: Effects of acute sleep deprivation on individuals across different APOE genotypes: a randomized controlled trial protocol.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial protocol describes a study to assess the effects of 24-hour acute sleep deprivation on plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers (Aβ42, Aβ40, t-tau, p-tau181, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP) in 60 healthy young adults stratified by APOE genotype (ε3/ε3, ε4 carriers, ε2 carriers). It aims to test APOE genotype-dependent biomarker responses and includes exploratory proteomics, metabolomics, and PET/MRI outcomes.

papers.title: Circadian and Sex-Specific Responses to Alternaria alternata in Allergic Airway Inflammation
papers.summary: In a preclinical mouse model, Alternaria alternata-induced allergic airway inflammation, airway hyperresponsiveness, and epithelial barrier disruption were found to depend on circadian time and sex, with female mice showing greater inflammation at ZT0 and males at ZT12. The study links these responses to IL-33, ILC2/Th2 accumulation, STAT activation, and altered clock protein expression, suggesting chronotherapeutic approaches for asthma.

papers.title: REV-ERBs as regulators of circadian rhythm, neuroinflammation, and glial lipid homeostasis in Alzheimer's disease. A narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that REV-ERBα/β nuclear receptors integrate circadian, metabolic, and neuroimmune pathways in Alzheimer's disease, with preclinical data showing pan-REV-ERB agonists reduce glial activation, restore NCoR/HDAC3 repression, improve cognition, and partially realign circadian rhythms, though compounds have pharmacokinetic and off-target limitations.

papers.title: Tri-Stream Disentangled Network with Adaptive Dual-Space Fusion for Electroencephalography-Based Image Reconstruction on THINGS-EEG2.
papers.summary: The paper presents a protocol for the Tri-Stream Disentangled Network (TDE-Net), a computational framework for EEG-based image reconstruction that organizes EEG into raw anchor, functional graph, and temporal semantic streams. Evaluated on THINGS-EEG2, TDE-Net achieved a mean CLIP pairwise identification accuracy of 0.8135 across 10 participants.

papers.title: Olfactory impairment and probable REM sleep behavior disorder in Parkinson's disease: clinical relevance to the single- and dual-hit hypotheses.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 201 Parkinson's disease patients, probable RBD (pRBD) and anosmia co-occurrence was examined relative to single- and dual-hit hypotheses. Anosmia was associated with cognitive impairment in pRBD-negative but not pRBD-positive participants, and significant anosmia-by-pRBD interactions were found for motor severity and cognition, suggesting that combined olfactory and pRBD assessment may refine clinical phenotyping.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG and EEG-Derived Markers of Severity, Prognosis, and Recovery After Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 33 studies (1,696 stroke or suspected-stroke participants) found that greater EEG/QEEG abnormality—especially increased slow-wave activity and higher delta/alpha or delta-theta/alpha-beta ratios—was consistently associated with greater severity, larger lesion burden, and poorer functional outcomes, but evidence was heterogeneous with low to very-low certainty and no universal prognostic threshold could be supported.

papers.title: Movement and Frontal Theta Activity During Step-Based Exergaming in Healthy Younger and Older Adults: Laboratory-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional laboratory study investigated how movement and frontal theta activity relate to game performance in a step-based exergame among 32 healthy younger and older adults. Game scores were strongly positively correlated with movement (vector magnitude) across all levels and age groups, while frontal theta activity showed limited and non-significant associations with performance, suggesting that game scores primarily reflect movement output rather than cognitive-control demands.

papers.title: Aerospace stressors and brain health in military aviators: a glymphatic-neurovascular framework.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes a glymphatic-neurovascular framework in which military aviation stressors (hypobaria, intermittent hypoxia/hyperoxia, high +Gz, sleep/circadian disruption, wakefulness-promoting agents, noise, radiation, chemicals) may converge on neurovascular, blood-brain barrier, perivascular, and inflammatory pathways, while noting that direct human evidence of glymphatic dysfunction in aviators is absent and calling for exposure-resolved longitudinal research.

papers.title: Feature-Engineering Strategies for EEG-Based ADHD Classification in Children: A Controlled Benchmark of Expert, LLM-Guided and Full-Space Comparators
papers.summary: This benchmark compared expert-reconstructed, LLM-guided, and full-space feature strategies for EEG-based ADHD classification in 77 children under leakage-controlled subject-level validation. Expert-reconstructed features with random forest achieved 71.4% accuracy in LOOCV, while no consistent advantage was found for LLM-guided features, and strict artifact gating reduced accuracy below the no-information rate.

papers.title: Tanshinone IIA Ameliorates Sleep Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment: Involvement of Gut Microbiota and the TLR4/NF-κB Signaling Pathway.
papers.journal: The American journal of Chinese medicine
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived rats, tanshinone IIA improved cognitive function, reduced hippocampal inflammation and neuronal death, and attenuated blood-brain barrier disruption, effects associated with gut microbiota regulation, reduced LPS leakage, and modulation of TLR4/NF-κB signaling.

papers.title: Sleep restriction induces histoarchitectural and cellular remodeling in the rat distal colon: a peripheral consequence of circadian disruption.
authors: Gláucia Eloisa Munhoz de Lion Siervo
papers.summary: Rats exposed to 21 days of sleep restriction showed increased mucosal thickness, crypt depth, goblet cell depletion, mast cell hyperplasia, and enteric neuro-glial remodeling in the distal colon, without macroscopic lesions. These findings suggest that intestinal remodeling is a peripheral consequence of circadian disruption.

papers.title: Maternal circadian rhythm writes immune fate in offspring.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses a recent Caenorhabditis elegans study showing that maternal circadian entrainment rhythmically alters offspring basal irg-5 expression and infection vulnerability, proposing mechanistic and evolutionary bet-hedging interpretations.

papers.title: Electroencephalography (EEG) and Quantitative EEG for Acute Stroke Triage and Post-Reperfusion Monitoring: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 15 studies found that EEG and quantitative EEG show candidate value for acute stroke triage and post-reperfusion monitoring, but evidence heterogeneity prevented pooled diagnostic accuracy estimates and certainty was very low to low.

papers.title: Effects of one night of sleep deprivation on single- and dual-task gait.
papers.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
papers.summary: In 18 healthy adults, one night of sleep deprivation increased step time and step length, reduced anteroposterior foot placement error and mediolateral margin of stability, but did not fully mimic dual-task gait effects. The findings suggest that sleep deprivation affects gait through mechanisms beyond reduced cognitive resources.

papers.title: ANGPTL2 and CP define complementary circadian-associated signals in atrial fibrillation: integrative transcriptomics and external validation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Integrative transcriptomics and external validation identified ANGPTL2 and CP as circadian-associated genes consistently upregulated in fibrillating atria, with distinct expression profiles and enrichment in vascular and stromal cell populations, but no compound met criteria for cross-cohort drug repurposing.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in drug-resistant epilepsy: A randomized, sham-controlled crossover trial with exploratory EEG and MRI response phenotyping.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled crossover pilot trial with 14 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients, active taVNS did not significantly outperform sham stimulation for seizure reduction (mean SRR 46.26% active vs 48.62% sham). Greater EEG beta-band attenuation in occipital and frontal regions was associated with larger active-specific benefit, while bilateral structural abnormalities and limbic involvement were more frequent among nonresponders.

papers.title: Circadian dysregulation of leptin and its role in skin inflammation and obesity: an integrative perspective.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on circadian leptin dysregulation linking meal timing and sleep disruption to obesity-associated skin inflammation, with a focus on psoriasis. It concludes that circadian leptin misalignment may represent a plausible upstream pathway, but direct causal evidence remains limited.

papers.title: The role of sleep and circadian rhythms in intervertebral disc degeneration.
papers.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
papers.summary: This narrative review examines bidirectional associations between sleep/circadian disturbances and intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), proposing five interconnected pathways including peripheral clock disruption and inflammation. It identifies CBT-I, exogenous melatonin, and morning bright light therapy as interventions with dual benefits for sleep and IDD.

papers.title: Pain profiles and their correlates among patients receiving medication for opioid use disorder: An exploratory study.
papers.journal: Journal of substance use and addiction treatment
papers.summary: This exploratory study of 211 patients receiving medication for opioid use disorder identified four pain profiles via k-means clustering, characterized by varying levels of pain, catastrophizing, and resilience. Profile D (moderate pain/catastrophizing, low resilience) had the least favorable pattern of individual, family, neighborhood, and social correlates.

papers.title: Diagnosing Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in adulthood: A scoping review of diagnostic challenges and age-related electroclinical evolution.
papers.summary: A scoping review of 45 sources encompassing 421 patients found that classical Lennox-Gastaut syndrome features are attenuated or under-documented in adulthood, with fulfillment of ILAE seizure-type criteria decreasing from 73% in childhood to 41% in adulthood and mandatory EEG hallmarks documented in less than half of adult patients. The authors recommend a longitudinal diagnostic mindset and age-adapted frameworks to avoid underdiagnosis.

papers.title: The SOMIRBD study one year later: feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary findings of a web-based screening model for isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: The SOMIRBD study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of web-based screening for isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) in 145 adults who completed an online questionnaire. Among 46 RBDSQ-positive participants, 14 underwent clinical assessment, leading to a clinical iRBD diagnosis in 2 (4.3% of all RBDSQ-positive participants), but the low specificity of RBDSQ highlighted the need for additional clinical information.

papers.title: Photoperiod-entrained circadian regulation of downstream transporter networks mediates nyctinastic leaf movement in peanut.
papers.summary: Combined temporal transcriptome profiling, photoperiod manipulation, and tissue-specific expression analysis in peanut to dissect molecular regulation of nyctinastic leaf movement. Identified rhythmic light- and circadian-related genes, including SWEET and aquaporin transporters and a pulvinus-enriched MYB transcription factor, supporting a model where photoreceptors and the circadian clock coordinate transporter and regulatory gene expression.

papers.title: Niosome-mediated melatonin delivery via SilMA/GelMA microneedles promotes healing of sleep deprivation-aggravated oral ulcers.
papers.summary: Develops a melatonin-loaded niosome-incorporated SilMA/GelMA composite hydrogel microneedle (Nio-MT@S-G MN) for localized delivery to oral ulcers aggravated by sleep deprivation. In vitro and in mice, the microneedle reduced neutrophil extracellular traps, restored epithelial barrier proteins, and significantly accelerated ulcer closure, identifying excessive NETs as a key mediator linking sleep deprivation to delayed oral wound healing.

papers.title: Global Research Trends in Sleep Quality, Sleep Deprivation and Sleep Promotion Among ICU Patients: A Descriptive and Evaluative Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.summary: A bibliometric analysis of 379 publications from 1983 to 2026 revealed a significant positive trend in ICU sleep research output and identified 'sleep', 'sleep deprivation', and 'delirium' as motor themes, with emerging concepts including circadian rhythm, actigraphy, fatigue, pain, and anxiety. The field's thematic structure guides targeted sleep promotion protocols in critical care.

papers.title: Effect of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on Postoperative Delirium in Older Patients Undergoing Carotid Endarterectomy: A Randomized Controlled Study.
papers.journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 65 older patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy, transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) significantly reduced the incidence and severity of postoperative delirium (POD) compared to control. TEAS also lowered optic nerve sheath diameter, Athens Insomnia Scale scores, and TNF-α levels, while increasing BDNF levels, suggesting links to reduced intracranial hypertension, improved sleep, and suppressed inflammation.

papers.title: Loneliness, problematic digital media use, and nutritional-metabolic vulnerability in adolescents from single-parent households: an integrative review of eating- and sleep-related pathways.
papers.summary: This integrative review synthesized evidence on loneliness and problematic digital media use as they relate to eating- and sleep-related behaviors in adolescents from single-parent households, proposing a contextual-behavioral vulnerability model. Direct evidence on single-parent adolescents was limited and mainly focused on family meals and weight outcomes, while broader evidence linked loneliness and digital media use to emotional eating, sleep disruption, and poor diet quality, with links to metabolic outcomes remaining largely indirect.

papers.title: The Thai version of the defense and veterans pain rating scale (DV-PRS) for postoperative pain assessment in patients after postpartum tubal ligation and total abdominal hysterectomy: a psychometric evaluation.
papers.summary: This psychometric validation study evaluated the Thai version of the Defense and Veterans Pain Rating Scale (DVPRS-Thai) in 288 women after postpartum tubal ligation or total abdominal hysterectomy. The scale showed high internal consistency (Cronbach's α=0.946), moderate-to-strong convergence with the modified Brief Pain Inventory, known-group validity, and responsiveness, with no ceiling effects and some floor effects in the postpartum tubal ligation group.

papers.title: Factors Associated with the Health Status of Caregivers of Community-dwelling Older Adults with Dementia in Japan: The Toyama Dementia Survey.
keywords: behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia
papers.summary: This cross-sectional survey of 75 caregiver-care recipient pairs in Toyama, Japan, found that 40% of family caregivers of older adults with dementia experienced physical health problems and 37.3% experienced mental health problems. Caregiver age 80 years or older was significantly associated with physical health problems (adjusted OR 13.46), and male caregivers reported more sleep deprivation than female caregivers.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
